## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ṭhita-sikkhāpada* ("Standing", Sekhiya 70) is a training rule for Buddhist monks preserved in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule belongs to the *sekhiya* class of regulations concerning proper etiquette and decorum, specifically in the context of teaching the Dhamma. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule possesses extensive parallels across early Buddhist monastic traditions. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to the monastic code proper (*Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* Sekhiya 70), the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and the parallel regulations for nuns in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Outside the Theravāda transmission, corresponding rules are found in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 92 matching passages across 44 other texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest alignments occur with other *Sekhiya* training rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga—most notably Sekhiya 65, Sekhiya 64, Sekhiya 66, Sekhiya 63, and Sekhiya 60—where formulaic segments (§0.1–1.9) covering origin narratives, pronouncements, and case analyses show very high similarity [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments meeting the score threshold of 10 are recorded by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
